themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Outbreak Signal
themes_detail.summary: East Harlem is experiencing a significant spike in food poisoning complaints this week with 5 reports versus a baseline of 0.8 per week—a 567% increase (z-score: 4.39)—suggesting a potential foodborne illness cluster requiring immediate public health investigation.
evidence: 5 food poisoning complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.39 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Community Board has standing request for 'other programs to address public health issues' (unfunded)
No recent news coverage or Reddit discussion suggests emerging, unreported story
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health to identify which restaurants/food vendors are linked to complaints and whether an investigation has been opened
Interview residents who filed complaints about symptoms, timing, and location of meals to identify potential common source

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Surge
themes_detail.summary: This week, East Harlem recorded 15 rodent complaints compared to a 7.4-per-week baseline—a 103% spike (z-score: 3.26)—signaling accelerating pest problems that align with long-standing community requests for sanitation improvements.
evidence: 15 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 3.26 indicates high statistical significance
Community Board has repeated, unfunded budget request: 'Increase Graffiti Removal/Cleaning' (Department of Sanitation)
1,750 residential noise complaints and 716 unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days suggest broader sanitation strain
reporting_angles: Map rodent complaints against sanitation collection schedules and street cleanliness to identify gaps in service coverage
Interview DSNY on whether staffing or equipment shortages are contributing to rodent problem escalation

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Jump 86%
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints across East Harlem this week reached 51 reports versus a 27.4-per-week average—an 86% increase (z-score: 2.89)—adding to the district's already-heavy 311 burden where noise is the top complaint category at 1,750 reports over 90 days.
evidence: 51 noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 27.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 2.89 indicates statistically significant spike
Noise (residential, street/sidewalk, general) comprises 2,972 of top 90-day complaints—nearly 28% of volume
Community Board has unfunded request for 'Hire additional traffic enforcement agents' (Police Department)
reporting_angles: Determine if this week's spike correlates with specific events, construction, or venue activity
Interview residents in high-complaint blocks about source of noise and NYPD response times

themes_detail.label: Elevator Service Failures Spike
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints surged to 5 reports 3 weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.8 per week—a 567% increase (z-score: 4.39)—indicating housing maintenance problems in a district already burdened with 1,677 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days.
evidence: 5 elevator complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.39 indicates high statistical significance
Heat/hot water complaints (1,677) and plumbing complaints (514) dominate 90-day dataset, suggesting systemic housing code violations
563 DOB filings in last 90 days (465 alterations) signal construction activity but unclear if code compliance is being enforced
reporting_angles: Cross-reference elevator complaints with DOB violation records to identify buildings with repeated failures
Interview tenants in affected buildings about landlord responsiveness and request Housing Preservation Division (HPD) audit of elevator maintenance compliance

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dog Complaints Peak
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints hit 4 reports 3 weeks ago versus a 0.5-per-week baseline—a 700% spike (z-score: 4.95)—marking the highest statistical anomaly in this week's data, though timing suggests this is not an active current emergency.
evidence: 4 unleashed dog complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.95 is highest statistical anomaly in dataset but event timing is 3 weeks old
No follow-up complaints in current week suggest issue may have resolved or been misreported
reporting_angles: Verify whether 3-week-old spike has persisted with NYPD Animal Care and Control; if resolved, determine what enforcement action was taken
If ongoing, identify specific parks or blocks where unleashed dogs remain a problem and interview residents about safety concerns
